evidence_basis: GSEM pre-submission forced-fill/no-fill matched implementation factor (clinical domain; numerical no-fill result unresolved)
MedExpMem residual harmful-memory outcomes after domain/similarity/relevance filtering (clinical domain)
RSCB-MC direct abstention ablation: false-positive memory injection 0.0% full versus 17.5% without abstention, with cumulative reward -31.740 versus -87.800 (coding-domain deterministic replay)
semantic_controls: all rejected + empty memory is valid
adopted memory with matching packet digest is valid
mixed candidates selecting only adopted memory is valid
interpretation: This promotes abstention preservation from an additive probe to a canonical companion runtime-admission protocol without modifying per-record failure_memory_validator_v2. It checks the transition from already-validated receiver decisions to actual memory injection: selected memories must be adopted, packet digests/current context/policy must match, and a force-nonempty fallback is invalid when no candidate was adopted.
scope_limit: The 14/14 result validates protocol semantics only. It does not establish autonomous-science benchmark improvement, and the GSEM no-fill numerical outcome remains unresolved.
